text_blocks.snippet: Common active scams reported across Central Illinois include fake local business impersonation, government and municipal text message cons, and rental or property fraud. Scammers frequently use spoofed phone numbers, lookalike search engine ads, and fraudulent letterheads to target residents.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake local business impersonation, government and municipal text message cons, and rental or property fraud

list.snippet: Garage Door Impostors: Scammers set up fake online ads and numbers pretending to be legitimate Central Illinois repair companies (such as providers in Bloomington, Peoria, and East Peoria), overcharging drastically or sabotaging equipment.

Municipal & City Impostors: Fraudsters mail fake invoices or notices using official-looking city letterheads—often targeting individuals who recently interacted with local zoning boards or public offices.

Fake Toll & Traffic Texts: Text messages falsely claiming to be from the State of Illinois or local transit agencies demand immediate payment for unpaid tolls or traffic violations under threat of license suspension.
Rental & Student Housing Fraud: Scammers lift photos of real properties to post fake online rental listings, targeting college students moving into the region for the school year.
Property Deed Fraud: Con artists attempt to illegally file fraudulent documents or manipulate property titles, prompting local county recorders to step up monitoring.
Verify Independently: Never use phone numbers found in random search ads or unsolicited texts. Look up official contact information directly from verified municipal or business websites.
Practice the Pause: If a caller or letter demands immediate panic-driven action or secrecy, step back and verify the claim through official channels.
Do Not Click Links: Ignore unprompted text messages about tolls, package deliveries, or traffic fines containing payment links.

Report Fraud: File complaints or check active alerts through the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois
or the Illinois Attorney General
.
